extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and patent examiners preparing or examining Sequence Listing XML files for patent applications (biotech/sequence disclosures)
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and content standards for preparing a Sequence Listing XML (WIPO ST.26 / 37 CFR 1.833) submitted with patent applications disclosing nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences (applicable to filings on/after July 1, 2022).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid duplicating Sequence Listing XML in drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Sequence Listing XML' should not be duplicated in the drawings; however a sequence may be depicted in a figure when certain sequence-associated characteristics (e.g., sticky ends, double-stranded features, similarity/homology, protein structural features like epitopes/interaction domains) are better conveyed graphically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an enumerated sequence is presented in a drawing, the sequence must still be included in the 'Sequence Listing XML' if it falls within the definition in 37 CFR 1.831(b); a sequence identifier (preceded by 'SEQ ID NO:X' or the like) must be used either in the drawing itself or in the Brief Description of the Drawings. Examples: double-stranded nucleic acid features (not representable in ST.26 XML), sticky ends, homology maps, protein epitopes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence Listing XML must be a single file encoded using Unicode UTF-8
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Sequence Listing XML' must be presented as a single file in XML 1.0 encoded using Unicode UTF-8, with character set restrictions consistent with WIPO Standard ST.26 (paragraphs 40, 41 and Annex IV).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain elements (ApplicantName, InventorName, InventionTitle, NonEnglishQualifier_value) may use any valid Unicode characters except control code points 0000-001F and 007F-009F; all other elements/attributes must be composed of printable characters from Unicode Basic Latin (U+0020 through U+007E). Reserved characters (", &, ', <, >) must be replaced by predefined entities (see separate criterion). See MPEP § 2413.01(a) and WIPO ST.26.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserved characters must be replaced by predefined XML entities; numeric character references prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: In an XML instance of a 'Sequence Listing XML', numeric character references must not be used and the reserved characters <, >, &, " and ' must be replaced by the corresponding predefined entities (<, >, &, ", ') when used in an attribute value or element content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The only permitted character entity references are the predefined entities set forth in WIPO ST.26 paragraph 41. See MPEP § 2413.01(a) for the reproduced table of reserved characters and predefined entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence Listing XML must be valid according to the DTD (ST.26 Annex II)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sequence Listing XML must be valid according to the Document Type Definition (DTD) as presented in WIPO Standard ST.26, Annex II.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conformance to the DTD dictates the structure and use of elements and attributes in the XML. Use of the WIPO Sequence tool will enable generation of a Sequence Listing XML that conforms to the ST.26 DTD. (MPEP § 2413.01(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence Listing XML must contain an XML declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: The first line of the XML instance must contain the XML declaration: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement derives from paragraph 39(a) of WIPO ST.26 and is incorporated in 37 CFR 1.833(b)(2)(i). See MPEP § 2413.01(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence Listing XML must contain a DOCTYPE declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: The second line of the XML instance must contain the document type (DOCTYPE) declaration as defined in WIPO ST.26 paragraph 39(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example DOCTYPE declaration reproduced in MPEP § 2413.01(d): <!DOCTYPE ST26SequenceListing PUBLIC "-//WIPO//DTD Sequence Listing 1.3//EN" "ST26SequenceListing_V1_3.dtd">.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence Listing XML must contain a root element with specified attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: The XML instance must include a root element as prescribed by WIPO ST.26 paragraph 43, and that root element must have certain attributes (dtdVersion, fileName, softwareName, softwareVersion, productionDate, originalFreeTextLanguageCode, nonEnglishFreeTextLanguageCode) with specified mandatory/optional status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attributes and their meanings: dtdVersion (mandatory; e.g., 'V1_3'), fileName (mandatory), softwareName (optional), softwareVersion (optional), productionDate (optional, format 'CCYY-MM-DD'), originalFreeTextLanguageCode (optional), nonEnglishFreeTextLanguageCode (mandatory when NonEnglishQualifier_value present). See MPEP § 2413.01(e) reproducing paragraph 43 of ST.26.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence Listing XML must contain a General Information part with specified bibliographic elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sequence Listing XML must include a general information part that complies with WIPO ST.26 paragraphs 45, 47, and 48, containing bibliographic elements such as ApplicationIdentification (IPOfficeCode, ApplicationNumberText, FilingDate), ApplicantFileReference, EarliestPriorityApplicationIdentification, ApplicantName, ApplicantNameLatin, InventorName, InventorNameLatin, InventionTitle, SequenceTotalQuantity, etc., with specified mandatory/optional status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of requirements: ApplicationIdentification mandatory when sequence listing furnished after application number assignment; ApplicantName mandatory (with ApplicantNameLatin mandatory where ApplicantName contains non-Latin characters); InventionTitle mandatory (title should be between two to seven words) and includes languageCode attributes. See reproduced List of Patent Application Information Elements in MPEP § 2413.01(f) (from ST.26 paragraph 45) for element-by-element mandatory/optional guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name and language code rules for Applicant/Inventor and InventionTitle
rubrics_metrics.description: ApplicantName and InventorName must be indicated as generally referred to in the filing language and must include the appropriate languageCode attribute; transliteration/translation to Latin characters is required for ApplicantNameLatin (mandatory when ApplicantName contains non-Latin characters) and may be provided for InventorNameLatin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: InventionTitle must be indicated in the language of filing; additional InventionTitle elements may be used for translations into other languages. Language codes follow ISO 639-1:2002 as referenced in ST.26 paragraph 9. See MPEP § 2413.01(f)/(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence data part must be present and follow ST.26 sections for sequence representation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sequence Listing XML must include a sequence data part that complies with the applicable paragraphs (50–55, 57, 58, 60–69, 71–78, 80–87, 89–98, and 100) of WIPO ST.26, representing nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences according to § 1.832.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sequence data part is composed of one or more SequenceData elements; each SequenceData element contains information about one sequence and must have a mandatory attribute sequenceIDNumber (the sequence identifier). See MPEP § 2413.01(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: INSDSeq dependent elements required for each sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: Each SequenceData element must contain a dependent INSDSeq element with mandatory dependent elements including INSDSeq_length (length of sequence), INSDSeq_moltype (molecule type), INSDSeq_division (indication related to patent application), INSDSeq_feature-table (list of annotations), and INSDSeq_sequence (the sequence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific rules: INSDSeq_division must be present with value 'PAT'; intentionally skipped sequences must be handled as specified (mandatory with no value or specific values such as '000' for INSDSeq_sequence?). INSDSeq_sequence must disclose the sequence using only the appropriate nucleotide/amino acid symbols (see Tables reproduced in MPEP § 2412.03) and must not include numbers, punctuation, or whitespace characters. See ST.26 paragraphs 52–55, 57.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature table required for every sequence (except intentionally skipped sequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: A feature table is required for every sequence (except intentionally skipped sequences) and is contained in the INSDSeq_feature-table element composed of one or more INSDFeature elements; each INSDFeature describes a single feature and consists of INSDFeature_key, INSDFeature_location, and INSDFeature_quals (qualifiers) as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: INSDFeature_key is a word/abbreviation indicating the feature (mandatory). INSDFeature_location is mandatory and must contain at least one location descriptor. INSDFeature_quals is mandatory where the feature key requires qualifiers (e.g., 'source'). See ST.26 paragraph 60–61 and MPEP § 2413.01(g) I. FEATURE TABLE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use only the exclusive listing of feature keys and associated qualifiers from ST.26 Annex I
rubrics_metrics.description: Feature keys and their associated qualifiers (including which qualifiers are mandatory/optional) must be chosen exclusively from the listings provided in Annex I of WIPO ST.26 — Section 5 for nucleotide sequences and Section 7 for amino acid sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not invent custom feature keys or qualifiers; consult Annex I for the complete, exclusive list and mandatory qualifier requirements. See MPEP § 2413.01(g) II. FEATURE KEYS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory 'source' feature key and handling of multiple sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'source' feature key is mandatory for all nucleotide sequences and amino acid sequences (except intentionally skipped sequences). Each sequence must have a single 'source' feature key spanning the entire sequence. If a sequence originates from multiple sources, describe additional sources using 'misc_feature' plus qualifier 'note' for nucleotide sequences and 'REGION' plus qualifier 'note' for amino acid sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure 'source' spans the entire sequence and add additional feature entries with appropriate keys/qualifiers to disclose multiple sources. See ST.26 paragraph 63 and MPEP § 2413.01(g) III/MANDATORY FEATURE KEYS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature location descriptors: syntax and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: INSDFeature_location must contain at least one location descriptor that defines a site or region on the sequence; allowed descriptors include single residue (x), span (x..y), residues before/after (<x, >x, <..y, x..>y), and nucleotide-only site between residues (x^y). Location descriptors must not reference residue numbers beyond the sequence length and use positive integers with x < y where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amino acid sequences must contain one and only one INSDFeature_location element. For nucleotide sequences, multiple location descriptors may be used with location operators for discontinuous features. See ST.26 paragraph 64–66 and MPEP § 2413.01(g) IV. Include examples such as use of '<' and '>' to indicate extension beyond specified residues; in XML replace '<' and '>' with < and >.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location operators for nucleotide sequences (join, order, complement) and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Nucleotide INSDFeature_location elements may include location operators: join(location,...) to place indicated locations end-to-end (implying biological joining), order(location,...) to indicate elements found in specified order without implying joining, and complement(location) to indicate the feature is on the complementary strand. join/order require at least two comma-separated descriptors; x^y site descriptors must not be used inside join/order; complement may combine with join or order but join and order cannot be combined together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'join' when residues are physically brought into contact (e.g., exons contributing to coding region). See ST.26 paragraphs 67–71 and MPEP § 2413.01(g) IV.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature qualifiers: value formats and exclusive qualifiers list
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualifiers supply auxiliary information about features and have three value formats: (a) free text, (b) controlled vocabulary/enumerated values (e.g., numbers/dates), and (c) sequences. The exclusive listing of qualifiers and required value formats for each feature key is provided in Annex I of WIPO ST.26 (Sections 6 and 8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a qualifier value is a sequence encompassed by 37 CFR 1.831(b), that sequence must itself be separately included in the Sequence Listing XML and assigned its own sequence identifier. See ST.26 paragraphs 72–74 and MPEP § 2413.01(g) V–VII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory feature qualifiers: 'organism' and 'mol_type' for 'source' and other qualifiers rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'source' feature key requires mandatory qualifiers including 'organism' and 'mol_type'. Some optional feature keys also require mandatory qualifiers as listed in Annex I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure required qualifiers are present for keys that mandate them (see Annex I). The 'organism' and 'mol_type' qualifiers have detailed rules (see separate criteria entries). See ST.26 paragraph 75 and MPEP § 2413.01(g) VI.

rubrics_metrics.name: INSDQualifier structure and 'id' attribute rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Each qualifier is represented by an INSDQualifier element containing dependent elements INSDQualifier_name and INSDQualifier_value (and where specified, NonEnglishQualifier_value elements) and may include an optional 'id' attribute. The 'id' attribute, when used, must start with the letter 'q' followed by a positive integer and be unique within the sequence listing file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: INSDQualifier_value and NonEnglishQualifier_value must be composed in characters as set forth in paragraph 40(b) or 40(a) respectively and must follow Annex I value formats. See ST.26 paragraph 76 and MPEP § 2413.01(g) VII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organism qualifier value rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for the 'organism' qualifier: if sequence is naturally occurring and source organism has Latin genus and species, that designation must be used; preferred English common name may be given in 'note' but not in 'organism'. If genus known but species unspecified, use 'Genus sp'. If Latin genus/species unknown, use 'unidentified' and put known taxonomic info in 'note'. If source lacks Latin genus/species (e.g., virus), use another acceptable scientific name. If sequence is not naturally occurring, use 'synthetic construct' and describe generation details in 'note'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select organism designations from a taxonomy database where possible. See ST.26 paragraphs 77–83 and MPEP § 2413.01(g) VIII for examples and handling guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: mol_type qualifier values for nucleotide and amino acid sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'mol_type' qualifier must disclose the molecule type. For nucleotide sequences the value must be one of: 'genomic DNA', 'genomic RNA', 'mRNA', 'tRNA', 'rRNA', 'other RNA', 'other DNA', 'transcribed RNA', 'viral cRNA', 'unassigned DNA', or 'unassigned RNA'. If organism is 'synthetic construct' the mol_type must be either 'other RNA' or 'other DNA'. For amino acid sequences the mol_type qualifier value is 'protein'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This qualifier is distinct from the INSDSeq_moltype element; follow the allowed enumerated values exactly. See ST.26 paragraph 84 and MPEP § 2413.01(g) VIII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free text qualifiers: format and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Free text is a value format for certain qualifiers presented as a descriptive text phrase or other specified format; consult Annex I for which qualifiers accept language-dependent free text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language-dependent free text qualifiers may need associated languageCode attributes and may use NonEnglishQualifier_value elements. See ST.26 paragraph 85 and MPEP § 2413.01(g) IX and § 2413.01(h) for definitions and handling.
